bull_bear.body:
- Commodity price volatility - polypropylene resin and crude oil — The first of the three risks the Company itself tabulates in 'KEY RISKS AND MITIGATION MEASURES'. It is the structural one for a converter: the entire product range (FIBCs, PP woven fabric and bags, BOPP laminated bags, PP box bags) is a polypropylene derivative, so resin cost is the dominant input and it tracks crude. The MD&A names 'volatility in polypropylene resin prices' and 'fluctuations in crude oil prices' as factors that may influence industry dynamics globally and 'may impact profitability and growth' in India, and the Future Outlook repeats raw material price volatility as a challenge. Stated mitigation: strategic sourcing, a diversified supplier base, inventory optimization and efficient production planning - all buffering measures, none of them a pass-through or hedging mechanism, and no pricing/escalation clause with customers is disclosed.
- Supply chain disruption — The Company's second tabulated risk. Mitigation stated: supplier diversification, long-term vendor relationships, inventory management and multiple logistics partnerships. It compounds with the export orientation - the MD&A separately flags logistics cost pressures as an industry-level factor, and its own macro section names the West Asia conflict and the Strait of Hormuz as threats to global trade routes and energy security, which is the specific corridor risk for an India-based exporter of bulky, low-value-density freight.
- Health, safety and environmental (HSE) risk in manufacturing — The Company's third tabulated risk. Mitigation stated: a comprehensive SHES framework, regular training, workplace inspections and compliance monitoring. No incident, injury, LTIFR or environmental non-compliance data is disclosed anywhere in the routed text, so the effectiveness of the framework cannot be assessed from this report.
- Geopolitical conflict and trade-policy fragmentation — Flagged repeatedly and in the Company's own voice, not only as macro colour. The MD&A cites the West Asia conflict, heightened uncertainty over energy security and global trade routes (particularly the Strait of Hormuz), resulting commodity-market and inflation volatility, and downside risks from geopolitical conflicts, trade fragmentation and supply chain disruptions; the Indian FIBC section adds 'global trade uncertainties'; and the Future Outlook names 'geopolitical uncertainties and evolving trade policies' as challenges. For an exporter this is a demand and tariff risk, not just a cost risk.
- Regulatory and environmental-compliance change in packaging — 'Evolving environmental regulations' are named as a factor that may continue to influence global FIBC industry dynamics, and 'regulatory changes' as a factor that may impact Indian profitability and growth. The same paragraph frames the sustainability shift - circular-economy principles, packaging-waste reduction, recyclability, customers in developed markets demanding environmentally responsible packaging - as something manufacturers must re-engineer products for. That is a product-obsolescence and re-certification risk carried at the Company's cost, and the AR discloses no recycled-content or reusable-product programme against it.
- Export and customer concentration exposure (NOT labelled a risk by the Company) — STRUCTURAL EXPOSURE INFERRED FROM DISCLOSED FACTS, flagged as such: the Company presents 'strong export presence with an established international customer base' as a STRENGTH and commits to 'expanding its export footprint', while separately conceding that global trade uncertainties may impact profitability. It never discloses export share of turnover, customer count, top-customer concentration, geography split or currency exposure, and there is no forex-risk paragraph in the routed text. The exposure is therefore real but unquantifiable from this annual report - which is itself the finding.
- Single-product-line concentration, and unrelated diversification as the answer to it — All disclosed manufacturing revenue comes from one polypropylene packaging family sold into industrial end-markets, with a polymer-agency activity for Indian Oil Corporation Limited alongside. Against that, the Members approved on 06 June 2025 an alteration of the Object Clause enabling real estate development, construction and infrastructure, engineering and project execution, property and facility management, DATA CENTRE development, warehousing and logistics, and manufacture/trading of engineering products, smart technology devices and IT products [PROVENANCE: Board's Report item 5, profile / capex_expansion bundles]. Those are unrelated to packaging and to each other; no project, capital plan, management capability or timeline is attached to any of them. Execution and capital-allocation risk here is not discussed by the Board at all.
- Group-structure change: exit from the only subsidiary, entry into an unrelated minority stake — A Share Purchase Agreement dated 15 July 2026 provides for sale of the ENTIRE 51.01% holding in Fibcorp Polyweave Private Limited, the Company's only and material subsidiary, within 180 days and subject to customary conditions - after which the Company has no subsidiary and the consolidated entity collapses into the standalone one. In the opposite direction, a 19.58% stake in Stilonn Valves and Controls Private Limited, an unrelated valves-and-controls business, was acquired on 22 May 2026 - a minority position carrying no control and, at 19.58%, sitting just under the 20% associate threshold. Both are post-balance-sheet events [PROVENANCE: Board's Report item 4, profile / capex_expansion bundles].
- Risk oversight is thin by the Company's own account — As on 31 March 2026 the Company is not required to constitute a Risk Management Committee under Regulation 21 of the SEBI LODR Regulations, and has not done so; oversight rests with the full Board, which 'periodically reviews the key risk areas and mitigation measures'. The entire risk disclosure in this annual report is a three-row risk/mitigation table plus a policy reference - there is no risk register, no ranking, no likelihood/impact assessment, no emerging-risk section and no BRSR material-issues table anywhere in the routed text.

- Diversify beyond packaging under an amended object clause: at the EGM of 06 June 2025 the Members approved altering the Memorandum's Object Clause to permit real estate development, construction and infrastructure projects, engineering and project execution services, property and facility management, data centre development, warehousing and logistics solutions, and manufacturing and trading of engineering products, smart technology devices and IT products - which the Company says it intends to leverage 'to explore new avenues of growth' while continuing its existing packaging operations. - Prune the group structure around that portfolio logic: a Share Purchase Agreement dated 15 July 2026 provides for the sale of the entire 51.01% stake in Fibcorp Polyweave Private Limited, the Company's only and material subsidiary, within 180 days. [PROVENANCE: Board's Report item 4, profile / capex_expansion bundles]
- Compete on customised, quality-certified packaging rather than commodity bags - 'delivering high-quality, customized packaging solutions while strengthening its market position through innovation, operational excellence, capacity expansion and sustainable manufacturing practices'. [PROVENANCE: MD&A Business Overview, profile / registry bundles]
- Use quality accreditation as the route into regulated end-markets - continue to leverage the BRC Packaging Certification, ISO certifications and other internationally recognised standards to strengthen presence in food, pharmaceutical and other quality-sensitive industries. [PROVENANCE: MD&A Future Outlook, profile / risks_esg bundles]
- Expand the export footprint and grow in both domestic and international markets, positioning against supply-chain diversification by global buyers towards India. [PROVENANCE: MD&A Future Outlook and Opportunities, profile / risks_esg bundles]
- Fund growth from retained earnings rather than payout - no dividend was recommended for FY26 so as to conserve resources for future growth, business expansion, working capital and financial resilience. [PROVENANCE: Board's Report item 3, profile / capex_expansion bundles]
- Keep sustainability inside the operating strategy - integrating ESG principles across operations, running the existing 500 kWp on-grid solar plant and committing to increased renewable energy adoption, efficient resource utilisation and waste minimisation. [PROVENANCE: MD&A Sustainability Overview, profile / risks_esg / registry bundles]
- Maintain the non-manufacturing polymer channel - continue the association with Indian Oil Corporation Limited as Del Credere Agent (DCA) and Dealer Owned Polymer Warehouse (DOPW) for polymer marketing in the Udaipur and Jaipur regions, described as contributing steadily to revenue streams. [PROVENANCE: Board's Report item 2, profile / capex_expansion bundles]
- Retention-first, with the reinvestment rationale stated explicitly. The Board recommended NO dividend on equity shares for FY 2025-26 'with a view to conserving the Company's resources for future growth, business expansion and strengthening its financial position', on the belief that retaining profits enhances the ability to support ongoing operations, meet working capital requirements, undertake future growth initiatives and improve overall financial resilience [Board's Report item 3, back-filled from the profile / capex_expansion bundles]. No amount was transferred to any Reserves during the year, and no deposits were accepted from the public. The stated investment philosophy is to combine stable, cash-generating businesses with high-growth opportunities: acted on post-year-end by taking a 19.58% stake in Stilonn Valves and Controls Private Limited on 22 May 2026 and by agreeing, under a Share Purchase Agreement dated 15 July 2026, to exit the entire 51.01% holding in the material subsidiary Fibcorp Polyweave Private Limited within 180 days. Equity capital was also raised during the year: the Board's Report describes an increase in the Authorised Share Capital together with a preferential allotment of Convertible Warrants, for which the Company states it obtained all necessary approvals from Members, stock exchanges and other regulatory authorities - the aggregate figure in that sentence cannot be attributed to either item because the routed text begins mid-word (see extraction notes), so it is not asserted here. On CSR, Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 was not applicable to the Company for FY26 and no CSR expenditure was required to be incurred, although a CSR Committee and a CSR Policy are in place. Governance framing around all of this: a Code of Conduct for the Board and Senior Management, a Vigil Mechanism / Whistle Blower Policy with direct access to the Chairperson of the Audit Committee, a Related Party Transaction Policy, a Nomination and Remuneration Policy, periodic Board / committee / individual director evaluation and familiarisation programmes for Independent Directors.
- Renewable energy already in operation: a 500 kWp on-grid solar power plant, described as supporting cleaner energy consumption and reducing the Company's carbon footprint. Verbatim unit 'kWp'; no generation, no share of total consumption and no site attribution is disclosed.
- Forward environmental commitment, unquantified: 'the Company will remain committed to reducing its environmental footprint through increased renewable energy adoption, efficient resource utilization, waste minimization and continuous improvement in environmental performance.' No target, no baseline year and no target year is attached to any limb of it.
- ESG is stated to be integrated into long-term strategy across operations, supported by investments in operational efficiency, environmental management, workplace health and safety and process improvements, under a governance structure with ongoing monitoring mechanisms.
- Safety: a comprehensive SHES (Safety, Health, Environment and Security) framework with regular training, workplace inspections and compliance monitoring, presented as the mitigation for health, safety and environmental risk.
- Workforce gender composition as on 31 March 2026, disclosed under diversity, equity and inclusion: 110 male employees, 4 female employees, 0 transgender employees. The '0' for transgender employees is a stated value, not a blank. This is the only headcount disclosure in the entire routed text and implies a heavily male workforce; no attrition, wage, training-hours or contract-labour data is given.
- POSH: a Policy on Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal of Sexual Harassment covering permanent, contractual, temporary and trainee employees, supported by duly constituted Internal Committees under the 2013 Act. NO complaint pertaining to sexual harassment was received during the year - a stated nil, not a blank.
- Compliance with the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, including amendments and rules, with a stated commitment to a safe, inclusive and supportive workplace.
- Vigil Mechanism / Whistle Blower Policy under Section 177(9)-(10), LODR Regulation 22 and PIT Regulation 9A, covering unethical behaviour, actual or suspected fraud and Code of Conduct violations, with direct access to the Chairperson of the Audit Committee and protection against victimisation of the whistle blower.
- Human capital: continued investment in employee development through training in technical skills, operational efficiency, safety awareness and compliance, with employees described as a key driver of sustainable growth.
- CSR - a stated absence, not an omission: the Company has constituted a CSR Committee and formulated a CSR Policy under Section 135, but the Section 135 provisions were NOT applicable to the Company for the financial year ended 2026, so no CSR expenditure was required to be incurred during the year [PROVENANCE: Board's Report item 19, strategy_outlook bundle].
- Internal controls: a framework of policies, standard operating procedures and periodic reviews by the Internal Auditor, Management and Audit Committee, with the Company stating that NO material weakness was observed in the design or operating effectiveness of its internal control systems during the year, and that internal financial controls over financial reporting are adequate and operating effectively.
- Governance hygiene stated for the year: compliance with Secretarial Standards SS-1 and SS-2; no unclaimed dividend or shares required to be transferred to the IEPF during the year; no shares with differential rights and no sweat-equity or employee share scheme issued; no application filed under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016; and no instance of one-time settlement with any bank or financial institution.

outlook.body: This annual report contains NO capex programme, NO capacity-addition project and NO commissioning or ramp-up timeline of any kind - a real finding, not a gap in the extraction. 'Capacity expansion' appears exactly once, and only as one of four generic levers in the Business Overview ('strengthening its market position through innovation, operational excellence, capacity expansion and sustainable manufacturing practices'), with no plant, no line, no product, no quantum and no date attached. The only physical asset with a stated size anywhere in the document is the 500 kWp on-grid solar power plant, and that is described as already operating ('the Company continues to benefit from its renewable energy initiatives, including the operation of its 500 kWp on-grid solar power plant'), not as an addition made or planned. What the Company is actually doing instead is reshaping its portfolio and its permitted scope. First, scope: at the Extra-Ordinary General Meeting of 06 June 2025 the Members approved an alteration of the Object Clause of the Memorandum of Association enabling real estate development, construction and infrastructure projects, engineering and project execution services, property and facility management, data centre development, warehousing and logistics solutions, and manufacturing and trading of engineering products, smart technology devices, IT products and allied activities - a very wide widening for a flexible-packaging converter, which the Company says it intends to leverage 'to explore new avenues of growth' while continuing its existing packaging operations. No project, site, investment or date has yet been attached to any of those new objects. Second, portfolio, via two post-balance-sheet transactions disclosed under Board's Report item 4 'Material Changes and Commitments': on 22 May 2026 the Company acquired 2,43,400 equity shares of Stilonn Valves and Controls Private Limited at Rs 123.30 per share for a total consideration of Rs 3,00,11,220, taking it to a 19.58% equity stake, stated to be aligned with a strategy of 'combining stable, cash-generating businesses with high-growth opportunities'; and on 15 July 2026 it entered into a Share Purchase Agreement to sell its ENTIRE 51.01% stake in Fibcorp Polyweave Private Limited, its material subsidiary, for a consideration of Rs 192.12 lakh, subject to customary conditions and proposed to be consummated within 180 days of execution, on completion of which Fibcorp ceases to be a subsidiary. During FY26 itself there was no change in the subsidiary companies and the Company had no joint venture or associate. Net of all this, the direction of travel disclosed for the packaging business is efficiency and mix (operational efficiency, cost optimisation, product innovation, leveraging BRC and ISO certifications to enter food and pharmaceutical grades, expanding the export footprint) rather than tonnage: there is no brownfield, no greenfield, no debottlenecking, no new line and no new site anywhere in the routed text.

outlook.body:
- Global FIBC market growth is the headline demand driver management leans on: the market is projected to grow from USD 6.4 billion in 2026 to USD 11.87 billion by 2036 at a 6.4% CAGR, an absolute opportunity of approximately USD 5.49 billion over 2026-2036, on cost efficiency, durability, handling convenience and suitability for bulk transport and storage. [PROVENANCE: MD&A Industry Overview, delivered in the profile / registry / capex_expansion bundles]
- India is presented as the fastest-growing FIBC market globally, at a 5.80% CAGR ahead of China's 5.20%, with the country-CAGR panel also listing Canada 4.8%, Turkey 4.5%, Japan 4.3%, United States 3.8% and Germany 3.5%. [PROVENANCE: MD&A Industry Overview panel; the panel is a bare list of percentages against country names with no stated period, so it is reproduced only as the document orders it]
- Indian demand is expected to be pulled by chemicals, pharmaceuticals, agriculture and food processing, supported by India's competitive manufacturing capabilities, cost advantages, skilled workforce and integration with global supply chains. [PROVENANCE: MD&A Indian FIBC Market Dynamics]
- Supply-chain diversification by global buyers is called out as an export opportunity, with India positioned as a preferred sourcing destination for FIBCs. [PROVENANCE: MD&A Opportunities]
- Sustainability is framed as a demand driver, not just a cost: circular-economy principles, packaging-waste reduction, recyclability and responsible resource utilisation are pushing manufacturers towards reusable, recyclable and technically advanced FIBCs, with customers in developed markets specifically seeking packaging that combines operational efficiency with environmental responsibility.
- Regulated end-markets are the stated mix lever - rising demand for specialised and compliant packaging in food and pharmaceutical sectors, which the Company intends to address with its BRC and ISO certifications.
- Margin levers management credits for FY26 and continues to pursue: enhanced operational efficiencies, disciplined cost management, improved manufacturing productivity and better control over operating expenses (figures deliberately not reproduced).
- Named headwinds to that demand narrative: volatility in polypropylene resin prices, fluctuations in crude oil prices, logistics cost pressures, evolving environmental regulations, regulatory changes and global trade uncertainties, which management says may impact profitability and growth.
- Macro backdrop the Company sets its outlook against (this bundle's own MD&A page): global GDP growth projected at 3.1% in 2026 and 3.2% in 2027 per the IMF World Economic Outlook April 2026; emerging markets and developing economies at 4.4% in 2025, moderating to 3.9% in 2026 and recovering to 4.2% in 2027; advanced economies around 1.9% in 2025 tapering to 1.7% by 2027.
- India macro: the IMF is cited for India growing 7.0% in 2026 and 6.4% in 2027, on strong domestic demand, resilient consumption, sustained infrastructure spending and growth in services and manufacturing - with continued infrastructure development, manufacturing-led growth initiatives, policy reforms and participation in global value chains expected to sustain expansion.
- Geopolitics is named explicitly as a swing factor: the West Asia conflict raised concerns over energy security and global trade routes, particularly the Strait of Hormuz, with the resulting commodity-market and inflation volatility posing risks to growth.

risks.note: The first of the three risks the Company itself tabulates in 'KEY RISKS AND MITIGATION MEASURES'. It is the structural one for a converter: the entire product range (FIBCs, PP woven fabric and bags, BOPP laminated bags, PP box bags) is a polypropylene derivative, so resin cost is the dominant input and it tracks crude. The MD&A names 'volatility in polypropylene resin prices' and 'fluctuations in crude oil prices' as factors that may influence industry dynamics globally and 'may impact profitability and growth' in India, and the Future Outlook repeats raw material price volatility as a challenge. Stated mitigation: strategic sourcing, a diversified supplier base, inventory optimization and efficient production planning - all buffering measures, none of them a pass-through or hedging mechanism, and no pricing/escalation clause with customers is disclosed.
risks.risk: Commodity price volatility - polypropylene resin and crude oil

risks.note: The Company's second tabulated risk. Mitigation stated: supplier diversification, long-term vendor relationships, inventory management and multiple logistics partnerships. It compounds with the export orientation - the MD&A separately flags logistics cost pressures as an industry-level factor, and its own macro section names the West Asia conflict and the Strait of Hormuz as threats to global trade routes and energy security, which is the specific corridor risk for an India-based exporter of bulky, low-value-density freight.

The Company's third tabulated risk. Mitigation stated: a comprehensive SHES framework, regular training, workplace inspections and compliance monitoring. No incident, injury, LTIFR or environmental non-compliance data is disclosed anywhere in the routed text, so the effectiveness of the framework cannot be assessed from this report.
risks.risk: Health, safety and environmental (HSE) risk in manufacturing

risks.note: Flagged repeatedly and in the Company's own voice, not only as macro colour. The MD&A cites the West Asia conflict, heightened uncertainty over energy security and global trade routes (particularly the Strait of Hormuz), resulting commodity-market and inflation volatility, and downside risks from geopolitical conflicts, trade fragmentation and supply chain disruptions; the Indian FIBC section adds 'global trade uncertainties'; and the Future Outlook names 'geopolitical uncertainties and evolving trade policies' as challenges. For an exporter this is a demand and tariff risk, not just a cost risk.

'Evolving environmental regulations' are named as a factor that may continue to influence global FIBC industry dynamics, and 'regulatory changes' as a factor that may impact Indian profitability and growth. The same paragraph frames the sustainability shift - circular-economy principles, packaging-waste reduction, recyclability, customers in developed markets demanding environmentally responsible packaging - as something manufacturers must re-engineer products for. That is a product-obsolescence and re-certification risk carried at the Company's cost, and the AR discloses no recycled-content or reusable-product programme against it.
risks.risk: Regulatory and environmental-compliance change in packaging

risks.note: STRUCTURAL EXPOSURE INFERRED FROM DISCLOSED FACTS, flagged as such: the Company presents 'strong export presence with an established international customer base' as a STRENGTH and commits to 'expanding its export footprint', while separately conceding that global trade uncertainties may impact profitability. risks.risk: Commodity price volatility - polypropylene resin and crude oil
risks.note: The first of the three risks the Company itself tabulates in 'KEY RISKS AND MITIGATION MEASURES'. It is the structural one for a converter: the entire product range (FIBCs, PP woven fabric and bags, BOPP laminated bags, PP box bags) is a polypropylene derivative, so resin cost is the dominant input and it tracks crude. The MD&A names 'volatility in polypropylene resin prices' and 'fluctuations in crude oil prices' as factors that may influence industry dynamics globally and 'may impact profitability and growth' in India, and the Future Outlook repeats raw material price volatility as a challenge. Stated mitigation: strategic sourcing, a diversified supplier base, inventory optimization and efficient production planning - all buffering measures, none of them a pass-through or hedging mechanism, and no pricing/escalation clause with customers is disclosed.

The Company's second tabulated risk. Mitigation stated: supplier diversification, long-term vendor relationships, inventory management and multiple logistics partnerships. It compounds with the export orientation - the MD&A separately flags logistics cost pressures as an industry-level factor, and its own macro section names the West Asia conflict and the Strait of Hormuz as threats to global trade routes and energy security, which is the specific corridor risk for an India-based exporter of bulky, low-value-density freight.

risks.risk: Health, safety and environmental (HSE) risk in manufacturing
risks.note: The Company's third tabulated risk. Mitigation stated: a comprehensive SHES framework, regular training, workplace inspections and compliance monitoring. No incident, injury, LTIFR or environmental non-compliance data is disclosed anywhere in the routed text, so the effectiveness of the framework cannot be assessed from this report.

Flagged repeatedly and in the Company's own voice, not only as macro colour. The MD&A cites the West Asia conflict, heightened uncertainty over energy security and global trade routes (particularly the Strait of Hormuz), resulting commodity-market and inflation volatility, and downside risks from geopolitical conflicts, trade fragmentation and supply chain disruptions; the Indian FIBC section adds 'global trade uncertainties'; and the Future Outlook names 'geopolitical uncertainties and evolving trade policies' as challenges. For an exporter this is a demand and tariff risk, not just a cost risk.

risks.risk: Regulatory and environmental-compliance change in packaging
risks.note: 'Evolving environmental regulations' are named as a factor that may continue to influence global FIBC industry dynamics, and 'regulatory changes' as a factor that may impact Indian profitability and growth. The same paragraph frames the sustainability shift - circular-economy principles, packaging-waste reduction, recyclability, customers in developed markets demanding environmentally responsible packaging - as something manufacturers must re-engineer products for. That is a product-obsolescence and re-certification risk carried at the Company's cost, and the AR discloses no recycled-content or reusable-product programme against it.

risks.risk: Export and customer concentration exposure (NOT labelled a risk by the Company)
risks.note: STRUCTURAL EXPOSURE INFERRED FROM DISCLOSED FACTS, flagged as such: the Company presents 'strong export presence with an established international customer base' as a STRENGTH and commits to 'expanding its export footprint', while separately conceding that global trade uncertainties may impact profitability. It never discloses export share of turnover, customer count, top-customer concentration, geography split or currency exposure, and there is no forex-risk paragraph in the routed text. The exposure is therefore real but unquantifiable from this annual report - which is itself the finding.

risks.risk: Single-product-line concentration, and unrelated diversification as the answer to it
risks.note: All disclosed manufacturing revenue comes from one polypropylene packaging family sold into industrial end-markets, with a polymer-agency activity for Indian Oil Corporation Limited alongside. Against that, the Members approved on 06 June 2025 an alteration of the Object Clause enabling real estate development, construction and infrastructure, engineering and project execution, property and facility management, DATA CENTRE development, warehousing and logistics, and manufacture/trading of engineering products, smart technology devices and IT products [PROVENANCE: Board's Report item 5, profile / capex_expansion bundles]. Execution and capital-allocation risk here is not discussed by the Board at all.

risks.note: A Share Purchase Agreement dated 15 July 2026 provides for sale of the ENTIRE 51.01% holding in Fibcorp Polyweave Private Limited, the Company's only and material subsidiary, within 180 days and subject to customary conditions - after which the Company has no subsidiary and the consolidated entity collapses into the standalone one. - Governance hygiene stated for the year: compliance with Secretarial Standards SS-1 and SS-2; no unclaimed dividend or shares required to be transferred to the IEPF during the year; no shares with differential rights and no sweat-equity or employee share scheme issued; no application filed under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016; and no instance of one-time settlement with any bank or financial institution.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: This annual report contains NO capex programme, NO capacity-addition project and NO commissioning or ramp-up timeline of any kind - a real finding, not a gap in the extraction. 'Capacity expansion' appears exactly once, and only as one of four generic levers in the Business Overview ('strengthening its market position through innovation, operational excellence, capacity expansion and sustainable manufacturing practices'), with no plant, no line, no product, no quantum and no date attached. The only physical asset with a stated size anywhere in the document is the 500 kWp on-grid solar power plant, and that is described as already operating ('the Company continues to benefit from its renewable energy initiatives, including the operation of its 500 kWp on-grid solar power plant'), not as an addition made or planned. What the Company is actually doing instead is reshaping its portfolio and its permitted scope. First, scope: at the Extra-Ordinary General Meeting of 06 June 2025 the Members approved an alteration of the Object Clause of the Memorandum of Association enabling real estate development, construction and infrastructure projects, engineering and project execution services, property and facility management, data centre development, warehousing and logistics solutions, and manufacturing and trading of engineering products, smart technology devices, IT products and allied activities - a very wide widening for a flexible-packaging converter, which the Company says it intends to leverage 'to explore new avenues of growth' while continuing its existing packaging operations. No project, site, investment or date has yet been attached to any of those new objects. Second, portfolio, via two post-balance-sheet transactions disclosed under Board's Report item 4 'Material Changes and Commitments': on 22 May 2026 the Company acquired 2,43,400 equity shares of Stilonn Valves and Controls Private Limited at Rs 123.30 per share for a total consideration of Rs 3,00,11,220, taking it to a 19.58% equity stake, stated to be aligned with a strategy of 'combining stable, cash-generating businesses with high-growth opportunities'; and on 15 July 2026 it entered into a Share Purchase Agreement to sell its ENTIRE 51.01% stake in Fibcorp Polyweave Private Limited, its material subsidiary, for a consideration of Rs 192.12 lakh, subject to customary conditions and proposed to be consummated within 180 days of execution, on completion of which Fibcorp ceases to be a subsidiary. During FY26 itself there was no change in the subsidiary companies and the Company had no joint venture or associate. Net of all this, the direction of travel disclosed for the packaging business is efficiency and mix (operational efficiency, cost optimisation, product innovation, leveraging BRC and ISO certifications to enter food and pharmaceutical grades, expanding the export footprint) rather than tonnage: there is no brownfield, no greenfield, no debottlenecking, no new line and no new site anywhere in the routed text.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Extensive experience in manufacturing FIBCs, PP/HDPE woven bags and other industrial packaging solutions - over 25 years of industry experience claimed
- Diversified product portfolio serving multiple industries, including chemicals, pharmaceuticals, food products, fertilizers and agriculture
- Strong export presence with an established international customer base
- Integrated manufacturing facilities supporting operational efficiency, quality assurance and customized solutions
- Quality accreditation as a route into regulated end-markets - BRC Packaging Certification plus ISO certifications, which management says it will leverage to strengthen its presence in food, pharmaceutical and other quality-sensitive industries
- Focus on sustainability through energy efficiency, responsible resource utilization and environmental management initiatives, including an operating 500 kWp on-grid solar plant
- A continuing agency relationship with Indian Oil Corporation Limited as Del Credere Agent and Dealer Owned Polymer Warehouse for polymer marketing in the Udaipur and Jaipur regions - a non-manufacturing revenue stream tied to the same polymer value chain
- Group backing - Aeroflex Enterprises Limited (formerly Sat Industries Limited) is disclosed as the ultimate holding company in the Ind AS 24 note

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Commodity price volatility - polypropylene resin and crude oil — The first of the three risks the Company itself tabulates in 'KEY RISKS AND MITIGATION MEASURES'. It is the structural one for a converter: the entire product range (FIBCs, PP woven fabric and bags, BOPP laminated bags, PP box bags) is a polypropylene derivative, so resin cost is the dominant input and it tracks crude. The MD&A names 'volatility in polypropylene resin prices' and 'fluctuations in crude oil prices' as factors that may influence industry dynamics globally and 'may impact profitability and growth' in India, and the Future Outlook repeats raw material price volatility as a challenge. Stated mitigation: strategic sourcing, a diversified supplier base, inventory optimization and efficient production planning - all buffering measures, none of them a pass-through or hedging mechanism, and no pricing/escalation clause with customers is disclosed.
- Supply chain disruption — The Company's second tabulated risk. Mitigation stated: supplier diversification, long-term vendor relationships, inventory management and multiple logistics partnerships. It compounds with the export orientation - the MD&A separately flags logistics cost pressures as an industry-level factor, and its own macro section names the West Asia conflict and the Strait of Hormuz as threats to global trade routes and energy security, which is the specific corridor risk for an India-based exporter of bulky, low-value-density freight.
- Health, safety and environmental (HSE) risk in manufacturing — The Company's third tabulated risk. Mitigation stated: a comprehensive SHES framework, regular training, workplace inspections and compliance monitoring. No incident, injury, LTIFR or environmental non-compliance data is disclosed anywhere in the routed text, so the effectiveness of the framework cannot be assessed from this report.
- Geopolitical conflict and trade-policy fragmentation — Flagged repeatedly and in the Company's own voice, not only as macro colour. The MD&A cites the West Asia conflict, heightened uncertainty over energy security and global trade routes (particularly the Strait of Hormuz), resulting commodity-market and inflation volatility, and downside risks from geopolitical conflicts, trade fragmentation and supply chain disruptions; the Indian FIBC section adds 'global trade uncertainties'; and the Future Outlook names 'geopolitical uncertainties and evolving trade policies' as challenges. For an exporter this is a demand and tariff risk, not just a cost risk.
- Regulatory and environmental-compliance change in packaging — 'Evolving environmental regulations' are named as a factor that may continue to influence global FIBC industry dynamics, and 'regulatory changes' as a factor that may impact Indian profitability and growth. The same paragraph frames the sustainability shift - circular-economy principles, packaging-waste reduction, recyclability, customers in developed markets demanding environmentally responsible packaging - as something manufacturers must re-engineer products for. That is a product-obsolescence and re-certification risk carried at the Company's cost, and the AR discloses no recycled-content or reusable-product programme against it.
- Export and customer concentration exposure (NOT labelled a risk by the Company) — STRUCTURAL EXPOSURE INFERRED FROM DISCLOSED FACTS, flagged as such: the Company presents 'strong export presence with an established international customer base' as a STRENGTH and commits to 'expanding its export footprint', while separately conceding that global trade uncertainties may impact profitability. It never discloses export share of turnover, customer count, top-customer concentration, geography split or currency exposure, and there is no forex-risk paragraph in the routed text. The exposure is therefore real but unquantifiable from this annual report - which is itself the finding.
- Single-product-line concentration, and unrelated diversification as the answer to it — All disclosed manufacturing revenue comes from one polypropylene packaging family sold into industrial end-markets, with a polymer-agency activity for Indian Oil Corporation Limited alongside. Against that, the Members approved on 06 June 2025 an alteration of the Object Clause enabling real estate development, construction and infrastructure, engineering and project execution, property and facility management, DATA CENTRE development, warehousing and logistics, and manufacture/trading of engineering products, smart technology devices and IT products [PROVENANCE: Board's Report item 5, profile / capex_expansion bundles]. Those are unrelated to packaging and to each other; no project, capital plan, management capability or timeline is attached to any of them. Execution and capital-allocation risk here is not discussed by the Board at all.
- Group-structure change: exit from the only subsidiary, entry into an unrelated minority stake — A Share Purchase Agreement dated 15 July 2026 provides for sale of the ENTIRE 51.01% holding in Fibcorp Polyweave Private Limited, the Company's only and material subsidiary, within 180 days and subject to customary conditions - after which the Company has no subsidiary and the consolidated entity collapses into the standalone one. In the opposite direction, a 19.58% stake in Stilonn Valves and Controls Private Limited, an unrelated valves-and-controls business, was acquired on 22 May 2026 - a minority position carrying no control and, at 19.58%, sitting just under the 20% associate threshold. Both are post-balance-sheet events [PROVENANCE: Board's Report item 4, profile / capex_expansion bundles].
- Risk oversight is thin by the Company's own account — As on 31 March 2026 the Company is not required to constitute a Risk Management Committee under Regulation 21 of the SEBI LODR Regulations, and has not done so; oversight rests with the full Board, which 'periodically reviews the key risk areas and mitigation measures'. The entire risk disclosure in this annual report is a three-row risk/mitigation table plus a policy reference - there is no risk register, no ranking, no likelihood/impact assessment, no emerging-risk section and no BRSR material-issues table anywhere in the routed text.
